located_point.method: Approximate. Pakistan Archaeology 2 (1965) Fig. 2 puts the prehistoric site north-west of the Karachi-Khairpur road (the National Highway), across the road from the hill carrying Kot Diji Fort. In the Sentinel-2 composite (renders at 3 km and 1.2 km, RGB) the fort hill is the white limestone ridge with dark wall lines near 27.346 N 68.707 E and the highway is the straight diagonal road north-west of it; the point lies about 250 m north-west of the road opposite the fort. The mound itself could not be delimited among fields and buildings.

sources.north_evidence: No north arrow is printed on the plan as scanned (title, scale '0 1 2 3 4 5 FEET' and excavation square labels only). Fig. 2 on PDF page 40 ('Kot Diji - The Prehistoric site and its environs') has an N arrow but shows only the outline of the site.
sources.status: inspected, not measured: no north arrow

notes: The only plan of the excavated architecture, Fig. 4 of Khan 1965, carries no north arrow, and Fig. 3 (excavated area on contours) has none either; no shared feature links them to the arrow on Fig. 2. The report (PDF page 43, OCR) states that the fortification wall of the citadel belongs to the Kot Dijian period and that 'There is no evidence to show that the Harappans also used the fortification wall', so the most prominent straight feature is pre-Harappan in any case.
unmeasurable_reason: Plan without a north arrow (Pakistan Archaeology 2, 1965, Fig. 4) and features not resolvable at 10 m in the imagery.
imagery_unmeasurable_reason: Features not resolvable at 10 m: the mound is not distinguishable from the surrounding fields and buildings, and no straight edge can be tied to excavated architecture.
